ai_explanation.concept_rule: Substitute the given inputs into the exponential function $f(x) = 2^{x-1}$.

subparts.stem: Graph $y = f(x)$ and its inverse function on the same set of axes.
subparts.final_answer: $Graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$ as reflection across $y = x$$

mark_breakdown.desc: State that the graph of f^-1(x) is the reflection of f(x) across y = x
Correct sketch of reflected curve passing through (1, 1) and (2, 2)

subparts.solution: The graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$ is the reflection of the graph $y = f(x)$ in the line $y = x$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The graph of the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$ is obtained by reflecting $y = f(x)$ across the line $y = x$.
step_by_step: Note that points $(1, 1)$ and $(2, 2)$ lie on $y = x$, so they remain invariant on the inverse graph.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Reflecting across the $x$-axis or $y$-axis instead of the line $y = x$.

subparts.stem: State the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$.

mark_breakdown.desc: State domain and range of f(x)
Domain of f^-1 is range of f, and range of f^-1 is domain of f

subparts.solution:
The domain of $f(x)$ is $\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R}\}$ and the range of $f(x)$ is $\{y \mid y > 0\}$.
$\therefore$ the domain of $f^{-1}(x)$ is $\{x \mid x > 0\}$ and the range of $f^{-1}(x)$ is $\{y \mid y \in \mathbb{R}\}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$, and the range of $f^{-1}$ is the domain of $f$.
step_by_step: Find the domain of $f(x)$: all real numbers, $\mathbb{R}$.
Find the range of $f(x)$: since $2^{x-1} > 0$, range is $y > 0$.
Swap them to find domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Keeping the variable as $y$ for domain or $x$ for range.
